about_hero_desc: Formiche d'Italia is the digital evolution of the FormiKey thesis, a research project dedicated to identifying Italian ants. The goal: making myrmecology accessible to everyone.
about_formikey_p1: FormiKey originates from the master's thesis "Interactive key for the identification of Italian Formicidae genera and the species of the city of Rome", presented by Francesco Simone Mensa in the 2016-2017 academic year at the Department of Sciences, Roma Tre University, MSc in Biodiversity and Ecosystem Management, under the supervision of Prof. Andrea Di Giulio.
about_formikey_p2: The thesis produced an interactive multi-access identification key based on morphological character matrices built with Mesquite software and the MOSCHweb platform. Unlike traditional dichotomous keys, FormiKey allows selecting characters in any order. The original matrices were subsequently validated by Dr. Fabrizio Rigato (Civic Museum of Natural History of Milan).

about_bio_francesco: Author of the FormiKey identification key and taxonomic data. Designed the morphological character matrices and curated the genus and species data for Italian ants.
about_bio_claude: Development of the website, platform, and interactive identification key. Implementation of the scoring system with error tolerance and information gain.
about_thanks_text: We thank Dr. Fabrizio Rigato (Civic Museum of Natural History of Milan) for validating the morphological matrices, and all Italian myrmecologists who have contributed to the knowledge of Italy's ant fauna.
about_source_formikey_desc: Original data from the research thesis
about_cta_desc: Formiche d'Italia is a growing project. If you're an Italian ant expert and want to contribute, claim your profile or contact us to suggest corrections.
about_formikey_p3: Formiche d'Italia extends the original thesis work (41 genera and 75 species) to cover the 42 genera and 7 subfamilies currently present in the Italian peninsula, with a focus on the 79 species documented in the city of Rome.

methods_subtitle: Technical documentation of the identification algorithm, data sources, and methodology underlying the platform.
methods_origin_desc: The taxonomic and morphological data underlying the key derive from the master's thesis of Francesco Simone Mensa (Roma Tre, 2016-2017). The matrices were validated by Dr. Fabrizio Rigato (MSNM, 2015).
methods_thesis_desc: Character matrices built with Mesquite in NEXUS format for 42 genera and 79 species from the city of Rome.
methods_checklist_desc: Primary taxonomic reference: 267 Italian species across 7 subfamilies and 42 genera.
methods_images_desc: Specimens from AntWeb.org (California Academy of Sciences, CC BY-SA 3.0). Anatomical illustrations by Maurizio Mei.
methods_matrix_desc: The key uses a matrix of 44 morphological characters for 42 genera. Each character is classified by:
methods_matrix_region: Body region: head, thorax (mesosoma), petiole, gaster, legs, antennae
methods_matrix_scope: Taxonomic scope: some characters are specific to a single subfamily
methods_matrix_polymorphism: Each cell contains one or more possible states (polymorphism support: {0, 1}). The value ? indicates missing data and is treated as compatible.
methods_algo_desc: Unlike traditional dichotomous keys, characters can be selected in any order and genera are not eliminated but ranked by compatibility.
methods_step1_desc: Each selection is weighted by the Shannon entropy (information gain) of the character at the time of selection. A character that splits genera evenly has high entropy (high diagnostic value).
methods_step1_formula: where p<sub>i</sub> is the frequency of state i among the remaining candidate genera
methods_step2_wtot: Wtot = sum of weights for characters where the genus has data
methods_step2_weff: Wtot,eff = effective total weight, including penalty for missing data
methods_step3_desc: When all selected characters belong to the same subfamily, the system infers an implicit subfamily. Genera from other subfamilies receive a higher penalty for missing data (factor 0.8 vs. 0.3).
methods_step4_desc: The user can set a tolerance (0-3 allowed mismatches). With tolerance 0 (default) a genus contradicting even a single character is excluded; raising it keeps contradicting genera visible, but marked (“contradicts: …”) and ranked below fully matching ones.
methods_step5_desc: After each selection, the system computes Shannon entropy for unused characters. The character with the highest entropy (maximum discriminating power) is highlighted as "Suggested character".
methods_ux_desc: The key provides four indicators to guide the user during identification.
methods_ux_progress_desc: Weighted combination (70/30) of candidate concentration and number of characters used.
methods_ux_diagnosis_desc: Confidence level (high/medium/low) based on the gap between the first and second candidate.
methods_ux_impact_desc: For each unselected state, shows how many genera would be excluded by the choice.
methods_ux_suggested_desc: The character with the highest entropy among unused ones, highlighted with ★.
methods_limit_1: The key operates at the genus level, not the species level.
methods_limit_2: Characters are defined for the worker caste. Queens and males would require separate matrices.
methods_limit_3: The matrices date from 2015-2017. Subsequent taxonomic revisions have not yet been integrated.
methods_limit_4: Species cover the city of Rome. Expansion to the entire Italian fauna is underway.

guide_subtitle: A practical guide to observing morphological characters and using the interactive identification key.
guide_morpho_subtitle: The 4 body regions to examine for genus identification.
guide_head_shape: Head shape (frontal view): elongate, quadrate, rounded
guide_head_antennae: Number of antennal segments and club shape
guide_meso_profile: Thorax profile in lateral view: convex, with spines, flat
guide_pet_segments: Number of segments: 1 node or 2 nodes (petiole + postpetiole)
guide_gaster_acidopore: Acidopore: circular opening fringed with setae (typical of Formicinae)
guide_gaster_sting: Sting: present in Ponerinae and Myrmicinae
guide_howto_title: How to use the interactive key
guide_step2: Select the geographic region (optional — narrows results)
guide_step3: Observe the suggested character (marked with ★) — the one that best separates the remaining genera
guide_step4: Select the character state observed in your specimen
guide_step5: Compatible genera are filtered in real time
guide_step6: If unsure of an observation, increase the error tolerance (default: 0)
guide_step7: Continue until the results narrow down to a few genera
guide_tip_workers: Always collect workers (the most common caste), not queens or winged males
guide_tip_preserve: Preserve in ethanol with a clear label (locality, date, habitat)
guide_tip_multiple: If possible, collect multiple specimens from the same colony
guide_tip_photos: Photograph from 3 angles: head (frontal), profile, dorsal
guide_cta_desc: The interactive key guides you step by step.
pests_subtitle: Found ants in your house? Before taking action, it helps to understand which species you are dealing with. Correct identification helps choose the most effective strategy.
pests_common_title: The most common species in Italian homes
pests_lasius_desc: The most common in domestic environments. Colonies nest in soil near foundations and enter homes seeking sugary food. Generally harmless.
pests_pharaonis_desc: An exotic honey-coloured species that forms multiple colonies in heated buildings. Difficult to eradicate because colonies fragment when disturbed.
pests_tapinoma_desc: Small, very fast dark ants. They nest in cracks and crevices. They emit an unpleasant odour when crushed.
pests_camponotus_desc: The largest. They nest in wood by excavating galleries (they do not eat it). May indicate structural moisture problems.
pests_step1_desc: Use the identification key or consult the genus pages.
pests_step2_desc: Follow the worker trails to locate the point of entry into the house.
pests_step3_desc: Store food in sealed containers and clean up crumbs and sugary residues.
pests_step4_desc: Close entry points with silicone or caulk.
pests_step5_desc: Often ineffective and harmful to the environment. Contact a professional if needed.
pests_warn_camponotus: Large black ants (Camponotus) emerging from structural wood
pests_warn_persistent: Persistent infestation despite removal of food sources
pests_eco_desc: Ants aerate the soil, disperse seeds, and control other insects. Over 267 species live in Italy, most of them exclusively in natural habitats.

roadmap_v12_peninsula_desc: From 79 species (Rome) to the ~160 of central-southern Italy, the first of the three macro-areas of the Italian fauna checklist
roadmap_v12_macroarea_desc: Narrow down candidates in the key based on the macro-area of observation — northern, central-southern or insular Italy — following the Italian fauna checklist
roadmap_v12_new_records_desc: Addition of T. siculus, T. apenninicus, T. marae, T. poldii and T. vivianoi, described after 2022
roadmap_v2_species_key_desc: Extension of the key from genus to species level, starting from the species of central-southern Italy
roadmap_v21_model_desc: Deployment of model v2.5 (227 Italian species, val_top1 ~78%) as a pre-filter that narrows candidates before the morphological key. Output: top-5 species with confidence scores
roadmap_v21_iteration_desc: New model versions are trained offline and silently swapped in when they improve val_acc
roadmap_v21_compare_desc: Deep-zoom on images to compare two candidate species side by side
roadmap_v22_species_desc: Complete coverage of the Schifani 2022 checklist (267 species in 7 subfamilies)
roadmap_v22_matrix_desc: Universal characters to discriminate the subfamily first, then the genus
